questions.title: Tangents at 90°, radius 4 cm: find OP
questions.text: If PQ and PR are tangents to the circle with centre O and radius 4 cm such that ∠QPR = 90°, then the length OP is:
steps: ① Join OQ and OR: both are radii = 4 cm
③ ∠QPR = 90° too ⟹ OQPR has all angles 90°
④ Tangents from P are equal: PQ = PR = 4 cm ⟹ OQPR is a square
questions.remember: Radius ⊥ tangent at the point of contact. Tangents from one outside point are equal.
questions.trap: Picking 8 cm (4 + 4). OP is the diagonal of the square, not two sides added.
questions.tryit: Tangents from P make 90° with each other; OP = 10√2 cm. Find the radius.

questions.title: Radius 6, OP = 10: area of PQOR
questions.text: PQ and PR are tangents drawn from an external point P to a circle with centre O and radius 6 cm. If OP = 10 cm, then the area of the quadrilateral PQOR is:
steps: ④ △ORP is the same size (PR = PQ, OR = OQ)
questions.remember: Split the kite PQOR along OP into two equal right triangles.
questions.trap: Doing 6 × 8 = 48 and stopping happens to work here, but say why: it's 2 × (½ × 6 × 8).
questions.tryit: Radius 5 cm, OP = 13 cm. Find the area of PQOR.

questions.title: ∠POQ = 120°: find ∠PTQ
questions.text: TP and TQ are tangents drawn from an external point T to a circle with centre O. If ∠POQ = 120°, then ∠PTQ is:
steps: ② Quadrilateral OPTQ: angles add up to 360°
questions.remember: Angle between the tangents + angle at the centre = 180°.
questions.trap: Taking ∠PTQ = ½ × 120°. That's a different rule (angle at the circle), not this one.
questions.tryit: If the tangents from T meet at 70°, find ∠POQ.

questions.title: Assertion–Reason: radius is the shortest distance
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The radius is the smallest distance of a tangent from the centre of the circle.
Reason (R): The radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact.
opts: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
steps: R: radius ⊥ tangent at the point of contact  ✓ true
Any other point B on the tangent lies OUTSIDE the circle
⟹ the radius is the shortest distance  ✓ A true
Shortest distance to a line = the perpendicular, which is R
questions.remember: The shortest distance from a point to a line is the perpendicular. The radius is that perpendicular.
questions.trap: Choosing (b). R is exactly the reason A is true, so it IS the correct explanation.
questions.tryit: How many tangents can a circle have at one point on it?

questions.title: Circle inside a right triangle: legs 8 and 15
questions.text: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle ABC, right-angled at B, with AB = 8 cm and BC = 15 cm. Find the radius of the circle.
steps: ② Radii to AB and BC + angle B = 90° ⟹ a square of side r at B
③ So the tangents from A = 8 − r, from C = 15 − r
④ Tangents are equal ⟹ AC = (8 − r) + (15 − r)
questions.remember: Right triangle with legs a, b and hypotenuse c: inradius r = (a + b − c)/2.
questions.trap: Using r = (a + b + c)/2. That's the semi-perimeter, not the radius.
questions.tryit: Legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Find the inradius.

questions.title: Chord 24 cm, radius 15 cm: tangent length PA
questions.text: AB is a chord of length 24 cm of a circle of radius 15 cm. The tangents at A and B intersect at a point P. Find the length PA.
steps: ① OP ⊥ AB at M, the mid-point ⟹ AM = 12 cm
④ In right △OAP, AM is the altitude ⟹ AM² = OM × MP
questions.remember: In a right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse h satisfies h² = (one part) × (other part).
questions.trap: Taking OP = OM + 15. P is outside the circle, so find MP properly.
questions.tryit: Chord 8 cm, radius 5 cm; tangents at its ends meet at P. Find PA.

questions.title: Prove: a parallelogram around a circle is a rhombus (5 marks)
questions.text: Prove that a parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
steps: Given: ABCD is a parallelogram; its sides touch the circle at P, Q, R, S
To prove: ABCD is a rhombus (all sides equal)
① Tangents from one point are equal: AP = AS, BP = BQ, CR = CQ, DR = DS
② Add: (AP + BP) + (CR + DR) = (AS + DS) + (BQ + CQ)
④ Parallelogram: AB = CD and AD = BC ⟹ 2AB = 2AD
⑤ AB = AD, so all four sides are equal
∴ ABCD is a rhombus. Hence proved.
questions.ans: AB = BC = CD = DA · Hence proved
questions.remember: Any quadrilateral around a circle: AB + CD = AD + BC (sum of opposite sides equal).
questions.trap: Writing 'AP = BP'. Tangents are equal only when they come from the SAME point.
questions.tryit: A quadrilateral ABCD circumscribes a circle; AB = 6, BC = 7, CD = 4. Find AD.

questions.title: Case study: Arjun and the meditation garden
questions.text:
A circular meditation garden has centre O and radius 9 m. Arjun stands at a point P, 18 m from O, and draws tangents PA and PB to the garden's boundary.
(i) Find ∠OAP.  (ii) Find the tangent length PA.
(iii) Find ∠APB and ∠AOB.
questions.remember: OP = 2 × radius ⟹ the angle at P is 30° on each side, 60° between the tangents.
questions.trap: Taking ∠APB = 30°. That's only half of it: ∠APO. Double it.
questions.tryit: Radius 5 m, OP = 10 m. Find the angle between the tangents.
